Utopia for the Golden Frog of Panama

2012
Modified refrigerator, Arduino, custom electronics, aquarium, living ecosystem, custom software

A refrigerator rebuilt as a biosecure habitat for the Panamanian golden frog (Atelopus zeteki), as a tactical critique of the conservation strategies for the species. Custom electronics regulate the temperature and humidity of a living ecosystem inside, which is monitored digitally and opened to citizen science, so that the ethical and practical problems of keeping an endangered species alive play out in a household appliance. Made with anthropologist Eben Kirksey and ecosystem designer Mike Khadavi, it was shown at Proteus Gowanus in Brooklyn as part of the Multispecies Salon. It is the subject of a chapter in The Multispecies Salon (Duke University Press, 2014), edited by Kirksey, and was featured in MAKE Magazine.
